studyDesign: VCE Physics Study Design 2023-2027 (Units 1 and 2: 2023-2027; Units 3 and 4: 2024-2027)
note: Accredited VCAA study design used for VCE Physics Units 3 and 4 from the 2024 examination onward, sourced directly from VCAA's own published study design document (www.vcaa.vic.edu.au/curriculum/vce-curriculum/vce-study-designs/physics/physics). Earlier examinations (2023 and before) were set against the previous VCE Physics Study Design, whose Units 3 and 4 Areas of Study differ substantially (e.g. no dedicated fields/motion structure) and must be mapped separately -- see study-design-2016.json.

units.title: How do fields explain motion and electricity?

areasOfStudy.title: How do physicists explain motion in two dimensions?
keyTopics: Newton's three laws of motion
coplanar forces in one and two dimensions
uniform circular motion (vehicle on a circular/banked road, object on a string)
satellite motion modelled as uniform circular motion
Newton's second law applied to vertical circular motion
projectile motion near Earth's surface
qualitative effect of air resistance
conservation of energy and momentum in one-dimensional isolated systems
impulse: FΔt = mΔv
work done by a force
work as area under a force-distance graph
kinetic energy
elastic and inelastic collisions
elastic potential energy and Hooke's Law
gravitational potential energy: Eg = mgΔh

areasOfStudy.title: How do things move without contact?
keyTopics: field model for gravitation, magnetism and electricity
field shapes and directions, attractive/repulsive effects, dipoles and monopoles
inverse square law for gravitational and electric fields about a point mass/charge
potential energy changes of a mass or charge moving in a field
magnetic fields of bar magnets, current-carrying wires, loops and solenoids
static vs changing fields; uniform vs non-uniform fields
electric field acceleration of a charge: F = qE, W = qV
magnetic force on a charged particle: F = qvB
radius of circular path of a charged particle in a magnetic field
gravitational field acceleration of a mass: Eg = mgΔh
force due to gravity and normal force for satellites in circular orbit
force on a current-carrying conductor: F = nIlB
simple DC motors, split-ring commutators, torque
particle accelerators and synchrotrons (linear acceleration + magnetic direction change)

areasOfStudy.title: How are fields used in electricity generation?
keyTopics: magnetic flux
electromagnetic induction and induced emf
AC voltage generation
DC generators (split-ring commutator) vs AC alternators (slip rings)
photovoltaic cells and the need for an inverter
sinusoidal AC voltage: frequency, period, amplitude, peak-to-peak voltage/current
root-mean-square (RMS) voltage and current
ideal transformer action
transmission losses across transmission lines

units.title: How have creative ideas and investigation revolutionised thinking in physics?

areasOfStudy.title: How has understanding about the physical world changed?
keyTopics: light as a transverse electromagnetic wave
standing waves and superposition
diffraction and the effect of gap/obstacle size
Young's double slit experiment and interference
quantised photon energy: E = hf
the photoelectric effect
limitations of the wave model of light
electron diffraction as evidence for wave-like matter
de Broglie wavelength
momentum of photons and matter
atomic absorption and emission line spectra
photon energy from spectral transitions: E = hf
Einstein's postulates of special relativity
the Michelson-Morley experiment
proper time and proper length
time dilation and length contraction
relativistic examples: muon decay, particle accelerators, GPS satellite corrections
mass-energy equivalence: E = mc², Etot = Ek + E0

areasOfStudy.title: How is scientific inquiry used to investigate fields, motion or light?
keyTopics: student-designed practical investigation design
independent, dependent and controlled variables
accuracy, precision, repeatability, reproducibility, resolution, validity
error and uncertainty
scientific poster presentation and science communication
evaluating evidence for a hypothesis, model or theory
logbook authentication of primary data
